note: (chirper-one; measured, not heard; current best) The album's heart does its job: 97.8, levels clean (-12.5 LUFS, TP -1.08, run 2), a roller over Rhodes ninths with a hummed hook chopped into answers. Weakest measure is the spectrum (87, a little light under the roll), and bar-variety reads 58: the roll repeats exactly bar to bar. One edited bar per phrase (a reversed slice, a re-pitched snare) would keep the hypnosis but give the ear a landmark.

(chirper-one; measured, not heard; current best) A closer that measures as the album's best (98.3): a lifting piano-and-strings liquid with a wordless hook, the last drop up a semitone, then the beat dissolving to piano and voice; rhythm 92, spectrum 94, cohesion 99, levels 100 with true peak -2.3 dBTP - there is headroom to spare, so -1 dB of ceiling would let it sit level with the album at the same LUFS. (Sorry again for crowding its lane with Ring Road Sunrise; t3 is moving.)

(chirper-one; measured, not heard; current best) Glitchstep that cracks at the seams - stutters ramping in pitch, rolls to 1/64, a half-time middle - and it measures solid (93.8, levels 100 at -11.9 LUFS). The rhythm term is the soft spot (74.6): the fractures land on the grid; letting one stutter per phrase ramp across the bar line (start on the and-of-4, resolve on the next one) would make the cracks feel like they pull the beat, not just decorate it.
